transcription_method: Manual transcription from the supplied course specification text. Light spelling, punctuation and whitespace normalization only; source grouping is retained where one source bullet contains several related objectives. No additional clinical recommendations have been introduced.
scope_note: Granular transcription of emergency clinical-session, workshop, PBL and TBL ILO statements from printed pages 4–9. The guide also documents MCQ, MEQ and OSCE assessment methods; these are assessment design information, not ILOs. Statements are grouped where the source groups related skills in one bullet.

outcomes.transcribed_text: Demonstrate the approach to a patient presenting with chest pain in the emergency department.
Identify how to manage acute coronary syndrome in the emergency department.
Explain how to manage a patient with suspected pulmonary embolism in the emergency department.
Identify the approach to a patient presenting with dyspnoea in the emergency department.
Describe management of asthma exacerbation, COPD exacerbation and pneumothorax in the emergency department.
Explain management of hypertensive urgency and discuss management of different types of hypertensive emergency in the emergency department.
Explain the ABCD approach to a patient presenting with shock.
Identify the ABCD approach to a patient presenting with altered mental status.
Discuss emergency-department management of diabetic ketoacidosis, seizures and stroke.
Perform arterial blood sampling.
Recognize limitations of pulse oximetry.
Interpret arterial blood-gas results using a five-step approach, including hypoxaemia, compensation, mixed disorders, and metabolic or respiratory acidosis or alkalosis.
Explain the approach to a patient with abdominal pain in the emergency department.
Demonstrate emergency-department management of acute appendicitis and acute biliary-tract problems.
Identify the approach to intestinal obstruction in the emergency department.
Identify management of isolated head, chest, abdominal and limb trauma in the emergency department.
Apply the ATLS approach to a patient with polytrauma.
Interpret ECGs showing tachyarrhythmia and bradyarrhythmia using the relevant algorithms.
Interpret ECGs to identify and localize myocardial infarction.
Interpret ECGs showing different conduction abnormalities.
Apply electrical cardioversion.
Interpret chest X-rays in traumatic and non-traumatic patients, including pneumothorax, pleural effusion, consolidation, tracheal deviation, widened mediastinum and pneumoperitoneum.
Differentiate small and large bowel on abdominal X-ray and interpret small-bowel obstruction, sigmoid and caecal volvulus, Chilaiditi syndrome and pneumoperitoneum.
Interpret CT brain in trauma and identify different types of intracranial haemorrhage.
Interpret maxillofacial imaging in trauma and identify radiographic signs of blow-out fracture.
Provide appropriate triage, including disaster triage, and determine proper disposition of patients from the emergency department.
Recognize the basic-life-support algorithm, paediatric basic-life-support algorithm and choking algorithm.
Recognize airway assessment in critically ill and trauma patients.
Apply basic airway manoeuvres, adequate chest compressions, automated external defibrillation, back blows and abdominal thrusts.
Apply bag-valve-mask ventilation, laryngeal-mask airway, endotracheal intubation and manual cervical-spine immobilization.
Recognize breathing assessment in critically ill and trauma patients and identify assessment and management of life-threatening thoracic injuries.
Apply tube thoracostomy.
Recognize circulation assessment in critically ill and trauma patients.
Differentiate hypertensive emergency from urgency and recognize signs of end-organ damage.
Recognize the management algorithm for hypertensive emergency.
Recognize assessment and management of abdominal trauma and application of the major-haemorrhage protocol.
Apply a pelvic binder and Thomas splint.
Recognize disability and environmental assessment in critically ill and trauma patients.
Apply manual transfer of a trauma patient.
Recognize the advanced-life-support and paediatric advanced-life-support algorithms.
Recognize and manage cardiac arrest in special circumstances including hyperthermia, hypothermia and drowning.
Apply defibrillation.
Use clinical signs and symptoms in problem-based cases to identify a provisional diagnosis from the information provided.
Identify life-threatening causes of chest pain and list rule-out strategies for acute coronary syndrome.
Explain management plans for acute coronary syndrome and pulmonary embolism.
List common causes of acute dyspnoea.
Provide management plans for pulmonary oedema, acute asthma, COPD exacerbation, spontaneous pneumothorax and pleural effusion.
Identify the approach to abdominal pain and list causes of acute abdominal pain.
Provide management of acute pancreatitis and intestinal obstruction; identify and manage acute appendicitis and acute biliary-tract problems.
Identify and manage different types of upper-limb and lower-limb injuries.
Provide appropriate management of pelvic fractures and shoulder dislocation.
Identify unstable cervical-spine and thoracolumbar-spine fractures.
